items.title: Bobby Hutcherson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: That was a different album, the Solo/Quartet with McCoy.

ctx.x: That sounds like a title that you used for one of your albums, The Kicker.
We did that album. We did – Herbie was on that Solo/Quartet album. That was a different album, the Solo/Quartet with McCoy.
Later on, when you were leading the quintet with Harold Land, you had a variety of pianists in that group: Chick Corea, Stanley Cowell, Joe Sample. Talk a little bit about any of those gentlemen?

items.title: Tyner McCoy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I get to be the drummer with Bobby Hutcherson and McCoy Tyner.

ctx.x: Let me just pull that out for the record (Manhattan Moods), this is one of my favorites. I play along with this record because there is no drummer, I get to be the drummer with Bobby Hutcherson and McCoy Tyner.
Oh yeah, Bobby. Look at that smile! That smile is captivating.
